current.text: He was traded to Toronto and takes Brandon Ingram's spot. He faces no punishment from the league ruling, and the trade is expected to go through.
He is a projected starter for Toronto next to Quickley, Barrett, Barnes and Poeltl, and he is in the expected closing five.
Much of the Toronto offense is expected to run through him. Usage should move to him and away from Barrett and Quickley.
His numbers should stay close to last season's, apart from normal age decline.
He is coming off one of his best and healthiest seasons in years.
Experts see him as a top 10 per-game player with a tight range: best case 4th, worst case 21st.
He is expected to miss time and play about 60 to 65 games.
He should play some back-to-backs but not all of them, and load management in Toronto is likely.
The Raptors have 15 back-to-backs this season, three of them in the fantasy playoffs.

Experts will not take him inside the top 40 in head-to-head and call an ADP of around 20 to 29 too high. They see round 4 or 5 as the right range and call him risky there. His ESPN ADP of 51 is value.
In an auction, Josh would pay no more than 24 USD for him.
He went for 20 USD in a recent auction mock draft.

durable.text: He has a degenerative knee condition with repeated surgeries in the same knee: meniscus, ACL and quad tendinopathy. He also carries ankle sprain risk.
Experts do not trust his knee to hold up. Injuries and load management are the main worries about him.
He is a high-usage scorer, with usage over 30 percent last season.
He is one of the best free throw shooters in recent memory.
He is a good and willing three-point shooter who makes decisions quickly.
Steals are his standout category and a league outlier. He has no weak category for his position.
As an often-injured player, he is worth a bit more in roto than in head-to-head.

note: Per game he fits every build, with outlier steals and strong FT% and points. Experts still will not take him inside the top 40 in H2H because of his knee, likely load management and an expected 60 to 65 games. Josh caps him at 24 USD and he went for 20 USD in a mock, which matches the 20 USD he cost in our league last season. That is far below Yahoo's 32.6 USD average cost and ESPN's 42 USD value, so bid around 20 to 24 USD and let him go above that. Early in the season, check how many back-to-backs he plays and his Yahoo Q status. The Raptors have three back-to-backs in our playoff weeks.
